_comment: Every key is optional. Delete the ones you do not need - the defaults below are what the skill uses when a key is missing. Any key can also be overridden for one run with an ORCH_<KEY> environment variable, e.g. ORCH_DEFAULT_CWD.
_default_cwd: the directory new sessions start in, and the project whose logs Podium reads. Default: the current directory.
_session_prefix: how Claude Code names sessions here, without the -xx suffix. Default: the lowercased basename of default_cwd.
_orchestrator_tab: the herdr tab label the orchestrator sits in. Default: orchestrator.
_accounts_tool: optional script that prints an OAuth token for a named account: <tool> token <name>. Leave empty and account switching is off - every pane uses the ambient login.
_panes_per_tab: most panes `spawn --group` puts in one tab before it opens `<group>-2`. A 30-row window gives each of six panes two rows, which breaks claude's dialogs. Default: 3.
_cdp_url: optional DevTools URL of the one shared Chrome that sessions drive (the browser lock guards it). `doctor` probes <cdp_url>/json/version when set. Default: empty, no probe.
_codex_model: model id every `--kind codex` pane starts on, passed as `codex -m <id>`. The ids this machine can use are the `slug` values in ~/.codex/models_cache.json. Default: gpt-6-astra (GPT-6-Astra, the newest).
_projects_dir: where Claude Code keeps session logs. Default: ~/.claude/projects.
_handoffs_dir: where handoff and task files are written. Default: ~/.claude/handoffs.
_board_dir: where Podium's state and generated page live. Default: <skill>/board.
_digest_repos: repos `board.py digest` reads this morning's commits from. Default: none.
_podium_slack_channel: channel every `board.py done` and `board.py show` also posts one line to, so the page can keep them behind a tab. Empty (the default) turns the Slack mirror off; PODIUM_SLACK=0 turns it off for one run.
_slack_lib: directory holding the shared `slack.py` those posts go through (routines/sessionlib here). Empty = no Slack mirror, whatever the channel says.
_group_colors: prompt-bar colour (`/color`) per herdr group, set by `orch.py spawn` before the first prompt and by `orch.py color --all`. Keys are group names, values one of red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, cyan, default; the empty key is the no-group fallback. Defaults: orchestrator red, channela purple, webapp blue, school green, orch yellow, other cyan.
_autopick_enabled: let `board.py autopick` apply the recommended pick on a question the asker marked --auto and nobody answered inside 24h. Default false: with it off, autopick refuses and says so, and --dry-run still prints what would have fired.
_space_order: the herdr sidebar order `orch.py space --order` sorts toward. The first entry is the seat's own space and is never moved - only later entries get relocated, and only the ones out of place. A `Slack` entry with no live workspace yet gets one created (see `jobs_view.py`). Anything live but not named here keeps its current relative position. Default: empty, `space --order` no-ops and says so.
_auto_close_enabled: let board_watch.py run `orch.py auto-close` for real every 30 min, closing a pane only when it was spawned by orch.py, is idle+DONE for 30+ min, has no open board question naming it, and its git worktree has nothing uncommitted or unpushed. Default false: with it off, `orch.py auto-close --dry-run` still prints what would close.
